questions.question: Which name does NOT refer to a convex mirror?
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors have other names: fisheye, spot, or bug-eye mirrors.

questions.question: Which is acceptable during a pre-trip tire inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 2/32 inch deep

questions.explanation: Front tires need tread depth of at least 4/32 inch. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Tires must not be worn, cracked, or mismatched in size. Tires from different makers are acceptable. Check air pressure is correct.

questions.question: When do large combination vehicles take the longest to stop?
questions.explanation: Empty vehicles take longer to stop than loaded ones. Without weight, the wheels have less grip on the road.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, the upper fifth wheel glide plate should be:

options.text: Folded under the lower fifth wheel
Securely bolted to the trailer frame
Connected to the emergency air line

questions.correctAnswerText: Securely bolted to the trailer frame
questions.explanation: Always perform a thorough pre-trip inspection. The glide plate on the upper fifth wheel must be securely bolted to the trailer frame.

questions.question: At highway speeds, look ahead at the road about ____ in front of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Watch 12 to 15 seconds ahead for hazards. At highway speeds, this equals about one quarter mile.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is needed to warm up the engine
Should be done on slippery surfaces

questions.explanation: Always accelerate smoothly and slowly. Rough acceleration causes mechanical damage.

questions.question: Fatigue:
questions.explanation: Driving tired is dangerous and increases crash risk. Plan ahead to avoid driving while fatigued.

questions.question: How do you test hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump brakes three times. Press the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump brakes three times. Press the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly move down.
Pump brakes three times. Press the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.
Pump brakes three times. Press the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should be easy to push down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump brakes three times. Press the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: Test hydraulic brakes by pumping the pedal three times, then pressing firmly for five seconds. The pedal must not move. Movement means there may be a leak.

questions.question: To test trailer service brakes:

options.text: Move forward slowly and apply brakes with the pedal
Back up slowly and apply brakes with the hand control
Back up slowly and apply brakes with the pedal
Move forward slowly and apply brakes with the hand control

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly and apply brakes with the hand control
questions.explanation: First check that the system has normal air pressure and release the parking brake. Then move forward slowly and use the hand control to apply brakes. You should feel the trailer brakes engage.

questions.question: If your trailer goes off course while backing, you should:

options.text: Pull forward, reposition, and back again
Get out and move the trailer by hand
Turn the wheel all the way left until it straightens

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward, reposition, and back again
questions.explanation: If the trailer goes off course while backing, pull forward to reposition your vehicle and then try backing again.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you best tell if a trailer is starting to skid?

options.text: Check your mirrors to see if the trailer has left its lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors to see if the trailer has left its lane.
questions.explanation: The easiest way to notice a trailer skidding is to watch it in your mirrors. Checking your mirrors lets you spot skidding as soon as it starts.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the air compressor breaks, both systems will stop working.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: Hold it with one hand so you can eat or drink.
Hold it with one hand, then switch to the other.
Crack it to improve your grip.

questions.explanation: To control your vehicle properly, hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency brakes is correct?

options.text: They are not required on trucks.
They are only required on trailers.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: What do you test by pulling out the trailer air supply control?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before you start driving. First make sure the trailer rolls freely. Then pull out the trailer air supply control or set it to "emergency." Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that make your vehicle stop are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: What does the emergency air line do?

options.text: It is controlled by the foot brake.
It is connected to the relay valves.
It supplies air to the trailer air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It supplies air to the trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks on combination vehicles and controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: When do spring brakes come on?

options.text: When too much air pressure is lost.
When you turn on a dashboard control.
When your tires have very little tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: When too much air pressure is lost.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes activate automatically when air pressure drops to an unsafe level. Do not wait for the spring brakes to activate. When you see the low pressure warning, safely leave the road and stop your vehicle while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: Is it good to look far ahead when driving?

options.text: No, because your current location is more important than the road ahead.

questions.explanation: When driving, look 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This gives you time to notice dangers early and react to them.
